guest.bio_context: Aurel completed high school and worked for a landscaper to learn the value of hard work before pursuing higher education. He attended community college through a joint program with Cuyamaca College, then transferred to San Diego State University where he specialized in civil engineering. He worked as an estimator for a midsize general contractor specializing in concrete paving in San Diego for approximately one and a half years, then transitioned to an estimator and project manager role at a demolition contractor before joining Granite, a large general contractor.

pending_qa.q: How did Aurel's experience in demolition construction differ from his previous estimating role?
pending_qa.r: As an estimator and project manager for a midsize demolition contractor, Aurel had to learn about heavy equipment, access requirements, and what types of equipment are allowed in different buildings due to emissions concerns to prevent carbon monoxide or carbon emissions from entering certain rooms where people could pass out. He valued learning from field crews and laborers, whom he believes are often not acknowledged but are excellent teachers.

pending_qa.q: What are the core values that Aurel values at Granite?
pending_qa.r: Granite has five core values, and Aurel particularly values safety, excellence, and inclusivity. He also values the team of hard workers that Granite has built and describes everyone as very knowledgeable. He is grateful for joining such a large general contractor and recognizes that working with large public and private projects requires whatever time and effort it takes for the job to get done, not just a seven to four schedule.

pending_qa.q: What operational challenge did Aurel face regarding public safety on a construction project?
pending_qa.r: A retired gentleman regularly rode his bike through an active construction zone without a helmet, despite traffic control redirecting pedestrians to a different route. Aurel had to stop him and explain that the area required PPE and that traffic control had established a new route for both public and worker safety. Eventually, the man respected the project rules and came back the next day complying with the requirements.

pending_qa.q: What is the importance of clear communication with vendors and subcontractors on construction projects?
pending_qa.r: Aurel explained that having a good relationship with the foreman and trucks allows for precise material ordering. When the foreman needs half a truck of material or two scoops from an excavator, they can adjust in real time. The foreman knows exactly how much material is needed by looking at the site, so he won't request extra. Clear communication prevents waste and ensures project efficiency.

pending_qa.q: How did Aurel and his team resolve a storm drain mainline design conflict?
pending_qa.r: The original design called for a storm drain mainline at a slope of 0.25% to 0.33%, but it would have run into an electrical conduit bank, creating a design issue. After potholes revealed the conflict was feasible, they proposed three options. They ultimately chose to move the mainline 10 feet south, add 45-degree pipe connectors, run it around the electrical conduit, and angle back into the mainline to work around the design issue.

pending_qa.q: What technology tool does Aurel recommend for earthwork modeling and why is it challenging?
pending_qa.r: Aurel recommends learning AgTech, an earthwork modeling program, because it is the most challenging software he has ever worked with. He deliberately added it as a goal because he believes performing difficult tasks makes you capable of easier ones. The program is finicky, not user friendly, but it taught him persistence, patience, and problem-solving beyond just asking questions.

pending_qa.q: How does contract management impact project delivery timelines and costs?
pending_qa.r: Aurel emphasizes going based on contracts, not words. If a contract states delivery in 14 weeks, he requires it in 14 weeks, not 14 weeks plus 10 seconds. Failure to meet contractual deadlines results in back charges. Similarly, when Granite misses project deadlines, liquidated damages apply, which can be very expensive and make or break a project.

pending_qa.q: What environmental compliance best practice does Aurel recommend to construction professionals?
pending_qa.r: Aurel recommends understanding rules and regulations from an environmental perspective because it will save a ton of money and represents best practices. He specifically recommends getting a QSP (Qualified SWPPP Practitioner) certification and drafting weekly BMP reports in coordination with a consultant, as these are necessary and not terribly expensive.
